note: The `learner-public.v1` fail-closed rules, one case each. Every case starts from `tree-without-excluded-roots.json` and adds exactly one violation, so the digest constant is never in doubt — only the classification is. Cross-checked against C3's shipped regression suite: the two implementations must refuse the same inputs, not merely agree on the accepted ones.

cases.name: unclassified-top-level-directory
cases.why: The classification table is exhaustive (spike §4.1). An unknown root fails closed rather than being hashed or ignored — hashing it would make the digest depend on files nobody agreed were public, and ignoring it would make the digest blind to them.

cases.name: unclassified-top-level-file
cases.why: `policy.json` is the only classified top-level FILE. A stray `README.md` is not covered by the directory list and must not slip through on the grounds of looking harmless.

cases.name: allowed-directory-name-used-as-a-file
cases.why: Directory-ness is part of the classification, not just the name. `skills` is an allowed DIRECTORY; a regular file called `skills` is not an allowed top-level file. A profile that matched on name alone would admit an arbitrary blob under any of the thirteen directory names.

cases.name: symlink-at-the-top-level
cases.why: The profile fails closed on symlinks rather than following them. Following would let a package hash bytes that live outside the tree entirely — including inside an excluded root, which is how a `secrets/` file re-enters a 'public' digest.

cases.name: symlink-nested-inside-a-contributing-root
cases.why: Same rule, one level down — the check is per entry, not per root. A profile that only screened top-level entries would admit `skills/alpha/link.md -> ../../secrets/token`.

cases.name: special-file-inside-a-contributing-root
cases.why: A fifo, socket, or device node has no stable bytes to hash. Reading one can also block forever, which turns a digest computation into a hang.

cases.name: symlink-inside-an-excluded-root-is-skipped-not-refused
cases.why: The mirror image, and the case a naive fail-closed implementation gets wrong. Excluded roots hold arbitrary bytes — a real `.git/` routinely contains symlinks — so the subtree must be skipped BEFORE classification runs. An implementation that screens every entry and then excludes would refuse every real learner tree. Digest equals the golden constant; the package is still not materializable.
